mainTopic: Does a מנחה offered שלא לשמה count for its owner according to רבי שמעון, and what is the logic behind his rule that a visibly false intent does no harm?
overview: The amud opens by finishing a proof from a פסוק: even a נדבה may not be deliberately changed, so after one service of a מנחה was done for the wrong purpose, the rest must still be done properly. Our משנה says a מנחה whose handful was taken שלא לשמה is כשר but does not count for the owner. A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון, who says it does count, because a מנחה's form shows what it really is, while all זבחים look alike. According to רב אשי's reading of רבי שמעון, our משנה can still follow him. According to רבה and רבא, it clearly does not. The גמרא then shows the contradiction in רבי שמעון's own words: another ברייתא says a voluntary מנחה is like an אשם, valid but not counting for the owner. רבה answers that a change of offering type still counts, but a change of owner does not. When אביי objects that the הקש makes no such distinction, רבה explains that רבי שמעון works from logic: a wrong intent the act proves false does no harm, while a hidden one disqualifies. The גמרא then tests this rule with cases of bird offerings, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Even a voluntary offering may not be changed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its proof from the פסוק with a rhetorical question: is one allowed to change how a נדבה is offered? Obviously not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And with a voluntary offering, is it allowed to change it? (Of course not!)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof that started before this section. It asks a question whose answer is obvious: you may not change the procedure of even a נדבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls an offering that was not done as vowed a נדבה. Even so, nobody may deliberately do a נדבה the wrong way. So once one service of a מנחה was done for the wrong purpose, the remaining services must still be done properly, for the right purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: A voluntary gift offering
Is it permitted? (a question expecting the answer 'no')
To change or deviate from the proper procedure

phrases.english: And a gift offering, is it permitted
phrases.notes: This finishes a proof from the פסוק in דברים 23:24, which calls an offering that was not done as vowed a נדבה.

phrases.english: to deviate with it?

steps.whatToRemember: Even after one service of a מנחה was done with the wrong intent, you must still do the rest of it properly.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the derivation from the פסוק that began before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That the remaining services of a מנחה must still be done for their proper purpose even after one was done wrongly.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק that calls an offering not done as vowed a נדבה, together with the obvious rule that a נדבה may not be deliberately changed.

steps.title: Does our משנה disagree with רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that our משנה is not like רבי שמעון, who rules in a ברייתא that מנחות whose handful was removed שלא לשמן even count for the owner's obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say our משנה is not like רבי שמעון? For a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון says, all מנחות whose handful was removed not for their own sake are כשר and they count for the owner as his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It suggests that our משנה argues with רבי שמעון, and it quotes a ברייתא to show his opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says such מנחות are כשר but do not count for the owner. רבי שמעון says they do count. So the two seem to disagree, and the גמרא wants to know whether our משנה really goes against רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (the גמרא offers a suggestion it may later reject)
Had the handful (קֹמֶץ) removed, a main service of a מנחה
Not for their own sake, meaning with intent for a different offering
Valid and may be offered
They count for the owner and fulfill his obligation

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'כשר' with 'counts for the owner.' Our משנה agrees the מנחה is כשר. The argument is only about whether the owner fulfilled his obligation.

phrases.english: Shall we say our mishna
is not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon,
as it is taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
All meal offerings whose handful was removed not for their sake
are fit, and they count for the owners as their obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the proof from the פסוק to a new question about who our משנה follows.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of our משנה that מנחות whose קמיצה was done שלא לשמן do not count for the owner.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון says explicitly that they do count, so the משנה seems to go against a known תנא.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's reason: each מנחה looks different
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון explains that מנחות are unlike זבחים, because the way a מנחה is made shows what type it really is, even if the wrong type was in mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: For מנחות are not like animal offerings. If someone takes the handful from a מחבת for the sake of a מרחשת, the way it was made proves it is a מחבת. If from a dry one for the sake of one mixed with oil, the way it was made proves it is a dry one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי שמעון's reasoning. He shows that a מנחה's physical form tells you what it is, so a wrong intention does not change it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מחבת and a מרחשת are made differently and look different. A dry מנחה has no oil, while a בלולה is mixed with oil. Since anyone can see what the מנחה really is, the wrong intention is ignored, and the offering still counts for the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: A מנחה made on a flat pan
A מנחה made in a deep pan
A dry מנחה with no oil
A מנחה mixed with oil
Its making proves what it is; its form shows its true identity

phrases.english: For meal offerings are not similar to slaughtered offerings,
since one who removes a handful from a pan offering for the sake of a deep-pan offering,
its preparation proves about it that it is a pan offering,
a dry one for the sake of one mixed with oil,
its preparation proves about it that it is a dry one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבי שמעון's ruling quoted in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because a מנחה's form shows its true type, a wrong intention during קמיצה does not change it, and it still counts for the owner.

steps.title: With animal offerings, only intention tells them apart
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון contrasts זבחים: every animal offering is slaughtered, has its blood collected and is sprinkled the same way, so nothing shows which offering it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with animal offerings it is not so. There is one way of slaughtering for all of them, one way of sprinkling for all of them, and one way of collecting the blood for all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes רבי שמעון's argument by showing why זבחים are different from מנחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since all animal offerings go through the same services in the same way, nothing visible marks which offering is which. Only the intention identifies it, so a wrong intention does affect a זבח and it does not count for the owner. This completes the contrast that explains why רבי שמעון treats מנחות differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Animal offerings
Slaughtering the animal
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח
Collecting the blood in a vessel

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון: a מנחה's form shows what it is, so it counts for the owner even שלא לשמה. A זבח looks the same as every other זבח, so intention decides. Our משנה seems to disagree, since it says such מנחות do not count for the owner.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא sets up the גמרא's next job: deciding whether our משנה really goes against רבי שמעון or whether the two can be reconciled.

phrases.english: But with slaughtered offerings it is not so,
there is one slaughter for all of them,
and one sprinkling for all of them,
and one collection for all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contrast begun in step 3 by explaining the זבחים side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animal offerings are all done the same way, so only intention identifies them. A זבח offered שלא לשמה therefore does not count for the owner.

steps.title: According to רב אשי, the משנה can still follow רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reads רבי שמעון narrowly: the מנחה counts only when the vessel alone was named. Our משנה is about naming a different type of מנחה, so it can match רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works out well according to רב אשי, who said: Here, where it counts, he took the handful from a pan offering 'for the sake of a deep pan.' There, where it does not count, he took the handful from a pan מנחה 'for the sake of a deep-pan מנחה.' Our משנה is about a מנחה offered for the sake of a different מנחה, so it does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא partly defends the idea that our משנה can follow רבי שמעון. It does this by using רב אשי's way of explaining רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון seems to say two opposite things about whether a wrongly-intended מנחה counts. רב אשי settles this by the exact wording. If the person mentioned only the vessel (מרחשת), it counts. If he mentioned a different type of מנחה (מנחת מרחשת), it does not count. Our משנה deals with naming another מנחה, so it fits the second case.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This works out fine' for one opinion. It usually comes before a 'but what about the other opinion?' question.
The handful of flour that the כהן removes from a מנחה
A flat pan; a מנחה baked on a flat griddle
A deep pan; a מנחה fried in a deep pan

phrases.english: This works out well according to Rav Ashi, who said:
Here, it is where he removes the handful of a pan offering for the sake of a deep pan,
phrases.notes: He named only the vessel, not a type of offering. So רבי שמעון says it still counts.

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן בְּקוֹמֵץ מִנְחַת מַחֲבַת לְשׁוּם מִנְחַת מַרְחֶשֶׁת –
phrases.english: there, it is where he removes the handful of a pan meal offering for the sake of a deep-pan meal offering.
Our Mishnah is about a meal offering for the sake of another meal offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 2 (that the משנה is not like רבי שמעון), but only according to רב אשי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: רבי שמעון's lenient ruling applies only when the vessel alone was named.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה contradicts רבי שמעון, who says a מנחה שלא לשמה counts for the owner.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רב אשי, the משנה is about naming a different מנחה, where even רבי שמעון agrees it does not count.

steps.title: But what about רבה and רבא?
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רבא settle רבי שמעון's statements in a different way. So how can our משנה fit רבי שמעון according to them?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבה and רבא, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. רב אשי's explanation works, but רבה and רבא explain רבי שמעון differently. It sets up the next step, which tries an answer using רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fix from Step 5 depends completely on רב אשי's reading. If רבה and רבא draw the line somewhere else, the משנה may still clash with רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What can be said?' A challenge meaning this opinion seems to have no answer.

phrases.english: But according to Rabba and Rava,
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרַבָּה וְרָבָא מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits Step 5's answer by pointing out it works only for רב אשי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that our משנה can follow רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה and רבא explain רבי שמעון's two rulings differently, so רב אשי's distinction is not available to them.

steps.title: Suggested answer: use רבה's distinction
steps.stepSummary: Someone might suggest using רבה's way: a change of offering type (שינוי קודש) counts, but a change of owner (שינוי בעלים) does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say it is like רבה's answer: here it is a change of the offering's type, and there it is a change of owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a possible answer using רבה's explanation of רבי שמעון. It does this only so it can knock the answer down in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה says רבי שמעון lets the מנחה count when it was offered for the sake of another type of offering (שינוי קודש). It does not count when it was offered for a different owner (שינוי בעלים). If our משנה were about a change of owner, it could match רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you would say.' It brings a possible answer that will usually be rejected.
Changing the type of offering in one's mind, for example a sinner's מנחה offered as a voluntary one
Changing the owner in one's mind, for example Reuven's offering intended for Shimon

phrases.english: And if you would say, as Rabba answers:
Here, it is a change of sanctity,
phrases.notes: This is the case where רבי שמעון says it counts for the owner.

phrases.english: there, it is a change of owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer Step 6's question using רבה's distinction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proposed distinction between a change of offering type and a change of owner
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No answer exists for רבה and רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Maybe the משנה is about a change of owner, where even רבי שמעון agrees it does not count.

steps.title: Rejected: the משנה is clearly about a change of offering type
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's own example is a sinner's מנחה offered as a voluntary one. That is a שינוי קודש, which רבה's רבי שמעון says does count. So the משנה cannot follow רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: But our משנה is a change of the offering's type! It teaches: 'How is it for its sake and not for its sake? For the sake of a sinner's מנחה and for the sake of a voluntary מנחה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggested answer from Step 7. It quotes the משנה's own example to show this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's answer works only if our משנה is about a change of owner. But the משנה describes switching from a sinner's מנחה to a voluntary מנחה, which is a change of type. In that case רבה's רבי שמעון says it counts, yet our משנה says it does not. So the clash with רבי שמעון comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: The מנחה brought by a poor sinner as his חטאת
A voluntary מנחה
Done first for its proper purpose and then for a different purpose

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, our משנה can follow רבי שמעון, because it involves naming a different type of מנחה. According to רבה, it cannot, because the משנה is a שינוי קודש, which רבי שמעון holds still counts.

phrases.english: But our Mishnah is a change of sanctity,
as it teaches: 'How is it for its sake and not for its sake?'
For the sake of a sinner's meal offering
and then for the sake of a voluntary meal offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer suggested in Step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The attempt to fit the משנה to רבי שמעון according to רבה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's own example is a change of offering type, not a change of owner.

steps.title: Trying again with רבא's way of settling רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests fitting our משנה to רבי שמעון using רבא's answer: a מנחה treated as another מנחה is one case, and a מנחה treated as an animal offering is a different case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe use רבא's answer: in one place רבי שמעון means a handful taken from a מנחה for the sake of another מנחה, and in the other place he means a handful taken for the sake of an animal offering.
steps.whatsHappening: After רבה's approach failed, the גמרא tries רבא's approach to see if our משנה can match רבי שמעון. This sets up the next step, where the idea will be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא settles רבי שמעון's two statements by the kind of wrong purpose involved. When a מנחה is treated as another מנחה, it counts for the owner. When a מנחה is treated as an animal offering (זבח), it does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Or alternatively; the גמרא is offering another option
Here... there; a way of settling a contradiction by saying each statement is about a different case
Taking the handful of flour from a מנחה, the main service of the מנחה
An animal offering

phrases.english: And alternatively, as Rava answers:
Here, where one takes a handful from a meal offering for the sake of a meal offering,
phrases.notes: This is the case where רבי שמעון says the מנחה does count for the owner.

phrases.english: there, where one takes a handful from a meal offering for the sake of an animal offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבה's approach was rejected in step 8, the גמרא tries the other approach, רבא's, from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: meal-for-meal compared with meal-for-animal-offering
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe רבא's split lets our משנה fit רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: This is only being proposed; the next step tests it.

steps.title: Our משנה is exactly a meal-for-meal case
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה's example treats a voluntary מנחה as a sinner's מנחה. That is a מנחה treated as another מנחה, which רבא's רבי שמעון says counts. So it cannot match.
steps.simpleTranslation: But our משנה is a case of a מנחה for the sake of another מנחה. It teaches "not for their sake and then for their sake," meaning for the sake of a voluntary מנחה and then for the sake of a sinner's מנחה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the attempt to use רבא's answer. The משנה's own example is the meal-for-meal case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבא, רבי שמעון holds that a מנחה treated as another מנחה does count for the owner. Our משנה uses that very kind of case, yet it does not give the result רבי שמעון would give. So רבא's way does not let the משנה follow רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Not for their sake and then for their sake; first the wrong purpose, then the right one
A voluntary מנחה that a person chooses to bring
A sinner's מנחה, brought as an atonement offering by a poor person

phrases.aramaic: הָא מַתְנִיתִין מִנְחָה לְשׁוּם מִנְחָה הִיא,
phrases.english: But our mishna is a case of a meal offering for the sake of a meal offering,
as it teaches: "Not for their sake and for their sake":

phrases.aramaic: לְשֵׁם מִנְחַת נְדָבָה לְשֵׁם מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא.
phrases.english: for the sake of a voluntary meal offering, and then for the sake of a sinner's meal offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מַתְנִיתִין מִנְחָה לְשׁוּם מִנְחָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion of step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using רבא's approach to fit our משנה to רבי שמעון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's example is the meal-for-meal case, which רבא's רבי שמעון treats differently from the משנה.

steps.title: According to רבה and רבא, the משנה is not like רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: Since neither רבה's way nor רבא's way works, the גמרא concludes that for them the משנה does not follow רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, according to רבה and רבא, it is clear that our משנה does not follow רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this discussion. Only רב אשי's approach lets the משנה match רבי שמעון. According to רבה and רבא, it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both attempts (steps 7-8 and steps 9-10) failed for the same reason: the משנה's example treats one מנחה as another, and in that case רבי שמעון, as רבה and רבא explain him, would rule differently. So the question from step 6 is answered by admitting the משנה is not רבי שמעון's view.

keyTerms.meaning: It is clear; the גמרא accepts a conclusion after the other options failed
Not like (a certain sage's) opinion

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי can fit the משנה to רבי שמעון. According to רבה and רבא, the משנה does not follow רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: Rather, according to Rabba and Rava,
it is clear that our mishna is not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the result of the failed attempts in steps 7-10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבה and רבא, our משנה does not follow רבי שמעון; only רב אשי's reading allows it to.

steps.title: The ברייתא behind the contradiction in רבי שמעון's words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a new section and quotes רבי שמעון's ברייתא: the פסוק compares the מנחה to both a חטאת and an אשם, so some מנחות are like one and some are like the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone pointed out a contradiction between two statements of רבי שמעון. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון says, "It is most holy, like the sin offering and like the guilt offering." This means some of them are like a sin offering, and some are like a guilt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back and shows the source of the contradiction in רבי שמעון's words that was discussed earlier. This step sets things up by quoting the first part of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון reads the פסוק as splitting the מנחות into two groups. One group follows the rules of a חטאת, and the other follows the rules of an אשם. The next step explains which מנחה belongs to which group.

keyTerms.meaning: And he contrasts; pointing out that two sources seem to contradict
Most holy, the highest level of offerings
Sin offering
Guilt offering

phrases.english: And one raises a contradiction between Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Shimon,
as it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Shimon says:
"It is most holy, like the sin offering and like the guilt offering":

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ מֵהֶן כְּחַטָּאת, וְיֵשׁ מֵהֶן כְּאָשָׁם.
phrases.english: some of them are like a sin offering, and some of them are like a guilt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section: it cites the source behind the contradiction in רבי שמעון's words that was used in steps 5-11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Based on the פסוק, some מנחות follow the rules of a חטאת and some follow the rules of an אשם.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's ruling in the ברייתא of step 2 that מנחות whose handful was removed שלא לשמן count for the owner.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This ברייתא of רבי שמעון compares the voluntary מנחה to an אשם, and step 14 concludes that it is valid but does not count for the owner. That clashes with his ruling in step 2 that such מנחות do count.

steps.title: Sinner's מנחה is like a חטאת, voluntary מנחה is like an אשם
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון explains: a sinner's מנחה whose handful was taken for the wrong purpose is disqualified, like a חטאת. A voluntary מנחה in the same situation stays valid, like an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: A sinner's מנחה is like a sin offering. So if he took its handful not for its own sake, it is disqualified, like a sin offering. A voluntary מנחה is like a guilt offering. So if he took its handful not for its own sake, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and shows which מנחה is like which offering, and what that means when the handful is taken for the wrong purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת slaughtered for the wrong purpose is disqualified, while an אשם slaughtered for the wrong purpose is still valid. רבי שמעון applies the same rule to the מנחות: the sinner's מנחה is disqualified, and the voluntary מנחה stays valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore
Disqualified; the offering cannot be brought
Valid; the offering may be brought

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'valid' (כשירה) means the offering may still be brought. Whether it also counts for the owner's obligation is a separate question; that is what the contradiction with רבי שמעון's other statement is about.

phrases.english: A sinner's meal offering is like a sin offering;
therefore, if he took its handful not for its own sake,
it is disqualified, like a sin offering.
A voluntary meal offering is like a guilt offering;
therefore, if he took its handful not for its own sake, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the general split from step 12 by naming which מנחה is in which group.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sinner's מנחה whose handful was taken for the wrong purpose is disqualified; a voluntary מנחה in the same case is valid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the comparison to an אשם. Step 14 extends that comparison to say the voluntary מנחה does not count for its owner, and that is the line that clashes with רבי שמעון's ruling in step 2.

steps.title: A voluntary מנחה is like an אשם: valid but does not count
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון's ברייתא concludes: just as an אשם offered for the wrong purpose is valid but does not count for its owner, so too a voluntary מנחה is valid but does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: And like an אשם: just as an אשם is valid but does not count for its owner, so too a voluntary מנחה is valid but does not count for its owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי שמעון's ברייתא and spells out how the voluntary מנחה is like an אשם. This line also sets up a problem the גמרא will deal with next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said a voluntary מנחה with a wrong-purpose handful stays valid, like an אשם. Now רבי שמעון adds a second part of the comparison: like an אשם, it still does not count toward the owner's obligation. That seems to clash with another teaching of רבי שמעון, where such מנחות do count, so רבה will have to settle it.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt offering; if offered for the wrong purpose it stays valid but does not count for its owner
Brings acceptance; here it means the offering counts toward the owner's obligation
A voluntary meal offering that a person brings by choice
Valid; the offering may still be brought on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Valid (כשר) and counting for the owner (מרצה) are two separate things. The offering is still brought properly, but the owner must bring another one to fulfill his obligation.

phrases.english: And like a guilt offering –
just as a guilt offering is valid but does not bring acceptance,
phrases.notes: 'Does not bring acceptance' means the owner has not yet fulfilled his obligation with it.

phrases.english: so too, a voluntary meal offering
is valid but does not bring acceptance.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְאָשָׁם מָה אָשָׁם כָּשֵׁר וְאֵינוֹ מְרַצֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי שמעון's comparison of a voluntary מנחה to an אשם that began in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A voluntary מנחה whose handful was taken for the wrong purpose is valid but does not count for its owner, like an אשם.

steps.title: רבה: wrong type of offering versus wrong owner
steps.stepSummary: רבה resolves the clash in רבי שמעון's view. When the wrong intent is about the type of offering (שינוי קודש), it counts. When the wrong intent is about the owner (שינוי בעלים), it does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: There is no difficulty. Here, the case is a change of the offering's type. There, the case is a change of owner.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the contradiction raised in step 12. He says each of רבי שמעון's two teachings is talking about a different kind of wrong intent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One teaching of רבי שמעון says these מנחות count for the owner, and this ברייתא says they do not. רבה splits the cases. If the כהן thought of it as a different kind of מנחה (שינוי קודש), it still counts. If he thought of it as belonging to a different person (שינוי בעלים), it does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the formula for resolving a contradiction
Change of sanctity: intending the offering as a different type of offering
Change of owner: intending the offering for someone other than its real owner

phrases.english: Rabba said: It is not difficult.
phrases.notes: He's answering the clash from step 12: the ברייתא in step 2 says these מנחות count for the owner, and this one says they don't.

phrases.english: Here, it is a change of sanctity,
phrases.notes: The כהן had in mind a different kind of offering.

phrases.english: there, it is a change of owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה, לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בְּשִׁינּוּי קוֹדֶשׁ, כָּאן בְּשִׁינּוּי בְּעָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the clash raised by step 14's ruling that a voluntary מנחה does not count.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each teaching refers to a different type of wrong intent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון seems to contradict himself about whether a wrong-purpose מנחה counts for its owner.
steps.terutzMaskana: A wrong type of offering still counts. A wrong owner does not count.

steps.title: אביי: the הקש does not make that distinction
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה. The disqualification for wrong intent comes from the הקש comparing מנחה to חטאת and אשם, and for those offerings both kinds of change are treated the same. So why should a מנחה be different?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: After all, the wrong intent that the תורה disqualifies is learned from a הקש. So what difference does it make whether it is a change of type or a change of owner?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's answer by pointing to where the rule comes from in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that wrong intent matters for a מנחה comes only from the הקש to חטאת and אשם. For a real אשם, both a change of type and a change of owner keep it from counting. If the מנחה learns everything from that הקש, it should also treat both changes the same, so רבה's split looks baseless.

keyTerms.meaning: Now consider; it opens an argument built on something already agreed
Intent; the כהן's thought while doing the service
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
A הקש: a comparison the פסוק makes between two things
What difference does it make to me; a rhetorical challenge

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Now consider: the intent that the Merciful One disqualifies
is from a comparison.
phrases.notes: This is the comparison of מנחה to חטאת and אשם from step 12.

phrases.english: What difference is it to me if it is a change of sanctity,
and what difference is it to me if it is a change of owner?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: מִכְּדֵי מַחְשָׁבָה דִּפְסַל רַחֲמָנָא הֶקֵּישָׁא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's distinction from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's split between שינוי קודש and שינוי בעלים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source of the rule is the הקש to חטאת and אשם. That source treats both kinds of change alike, so there is no basis for treating them differently in a מנחה.

steps.title: רבה: the distinction comes from logic, not from the הקש
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that רבי שמעון's principle מעשיה מוכיחין (the way it is prepared proves what it is) is a סברא, a logical rule. רבי שמעון bases rulings on the reason behind a פסוק, so logic can create a distinction the הקש alone would not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The principle 'its preparation proves it' that רבי שמעון says is a logical reasoning, because רבי שמעון explains the reason behind the פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends his distinction. It does not come from the הקש. It comes from רבי שמעון's logical principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that when the way a מנחה is made shows what it is, a wrong thought about its type is plainly false and does not take hold, so the מנחה still counts. That reasoning only works for the type of offering, because the preparation does not show who the owner is, so a wrong-owner thought still takes effect. Since רבי שמעון rules based on the reason behind the פסוק, this logic can override what the bare הקש would suggest.

keyTerms.meaning: Its preparation proves it; the way the offering is made shows what it is
Logical reasoning, as opposed to a rule learned from a פסוק
Interprets the reason behind the פסוק and rules based on that reason

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה, in רבי שמעון's view a wrong-type intent on a מנחה still lets it count, because 'its preparation proves it' is a logical rule. A wrong-owner intent does not count, because the preparation proves nothing about the owner.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a well-known feature of רבי שמעון: he rules based on the reasons behind the תורה's laws, which can shape a law more than a bare comparison does.

phrases.english: He said to him:
'Its preparation proves it,' which Rabbi Shimon says,
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון's idea is that how a מנחה is made shows what kind it is, so a wrong thought about its type does not change it.

phrases.english: is a logical reasoning,
for Rabbi Shimon interprets the reason of the verse.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַעֲשֶׂיהָ מוֹכִיחִין דְּקָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, סְבָרָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 16 and defends רבה's distinction from step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the source: the distinction rests on logic, not on the הקש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the wrong-intent rule comes from the הקש, all kinds of change should be treated alike.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון's logical principle מעשיה מוכיחין applies only to the type of offering, so a wrong-type intent still counts while a wrong-owner intent does not.

steps.title: Hidden wrong intent disqualifies, visible wrong intent does not
steps.stepSummary: רבה finishes his answer. The תורה disqualifies a wrong intent that cannot be seen in the act. It does not disqualify a wrong intent that the act itself proves false.
steps.simpleTranslation: A wrong intent that cannot be recognized, the Merciful One disqualified. A wrong intent that can be recognized, the Merciful One did not disqualify.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה completes his answer to אביי by stating the rule behind רבי שמעון's distinction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A change of owner (שינוי בעלים) leaves no visible sign, so it can mislead, and the תורה disqualifies it. A change of offering type (שינוי קודש) in a מנחה is contradicted by how the מנחה looks and is prepared, so everyone can see the intent is false, and it does no harm. This is the סברא of מעשיה מוכיחין put into a clear rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Intent or thought during the service, here a wrong intent
That is not recognizable, meaning the act gives no sign that the intent is false
That is recognizable, meaning the act itself shows the intent is false
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, only a hidden wrong intent (like a change of owner) disqualifies. A wrong intent that the act itself proves false (like a change of מנחה type) does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule becomes the test case for the challenges that follow in the list of the סימן.

phrases.english: An intent that is not recognizable [as false]
the Merciful One disqualified;
an intent that is recognizable [as false]
the Merciful One did not disqualify.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבה's answer from step 17 by stating the rule behind the סברא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical principle (סברא) that sets aside the plain הקש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי assumed the הקש to חטאת and אשם means both kinds of change must be treated the same for a מנחה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Visible false intent is harmless and hidden false intent disqualifies, so a change of type and a change of owner differ for a מנחה.

steps.title: A memory aid for the coming challenges
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a list of key words to help remember the order of the challenges against רבה's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory aid: burnt offering, burnt offering, pinched and squeezed, bird sin offering, most holy offerings, lighter holy offerings.)
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא lists short code words for the series of challenges it is about to bring against רבה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word stands for one upcoming challenge, in order. It has no argument of its own. It only helps the learner keep track of what is coming.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid, a list of key words for remembering the order of what follows
Pinched the bird's neck and squeezed out its blood
Offerings of the most holy level
Offerings of lighter holiness

phrases.english: (Mnemonic: Burnt offering, burnt offering,
pinched and squeezed, bird sin offering,
offerings of the most sacred order, offerings of lesser sanctity.)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a list of challenges to the rule stated in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. A list of key words for the upcoming challenges.

steps.title: A bird עולה pinched above for the sake of a bird חטאת should count
steps.stepSummary: If a visible false intent does no harm, then a bird עולה pinched at the high spot for the sake of a חטאת should count. The high spot shows it is an עולה, since a חטאת is done low.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, a bird burnt offering that he pinched above [the red line] for the sake of a bird sin offering should count for its owner! Its actions prove that it is a bird burnt offering, because if it were a bird sin offering, he would have done it below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה's rule with a case about bird offerings, the first item in the memory aid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird עולה is pinched above the red line on the altar, and a bird חטאת is pinched below it. So pinching above should 'prove' this is an עולה, and the intent for a חטאת should be visibly false and harmless. Yet the הלכה is that it does not count for its owner, which seems to go against רבה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so: introduces a problem that follows from the rule just stated
A bird burnt offering, done above the red line
A bird sin offering, normally done below the red line
Above or below the red line around the middle of the altar
It should be accepted, meaning it should count for its owner

phrases.english: But if so,
a bird burnt offering that he pinched above
phrases.notes: Above means above the red line that runs around the middle of the altar.

phrases.english: for the sake of a bird sin offering,
it should effect acceptance [for its owner]?
Its actions prove about it
that it is a bird burnt offering,
for if it were a bird sin offering
he would have performed it below.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבה's rule from step 18 on a case of bird offerings.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's rule that a wrong intent which is visibly false does not disqualify
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pinching above shows the bird is an עולה, so the חטאת intent is visibly false. By רבה's rule it should count for its owner, but the הלכה is that it does not.

steps.title: A bird חטאת pinched above is also valid, so nothing is proven
steps.stepSummary: The challenge is rejected. A bird חטאת pinched above is valid after the fact too, so pinching above does not prove the bird is an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say a bird sin offering cannot be done above? But the Master said: pinching anywhere on the altar is valid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the challenge by showing that the place of the pinching does not really prove anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a bird חטאת pinched anywhere on the altar is valid after the fact, a bird pinched above could still be a חטאת. So the false intent is not visible after all. It falls under the hidden, disqualifying kind, and רבה's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? Introduces a rhetorical question that rejects an assumption
Does it not exist? Here: is it not possible?
Pinching the back of a bird's neck with the fingernail, the way a bird offering is slaughtered
Valid, here meaning valid after the fact

steps.confusionAlert: Doing a bird חטאת below is still the proper way from the start. The point is only that if it was done above, it is still valid, so the high spot is not proof that it is an עולה.

phrases.english: Is that to say that a bird sin offering above
is not possible?
Didn't the Master say:
Pinching in any place on the altar is valid!
phrases.notes: This is talking about a bird חטאת. It is valid after the fact, even though it should be done below.

steps.triggerLanguage: אטו חטאת העוף למעלה מי ליתא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of step 20 by showing that its proof (the high spot) is not a real proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that pinching above shows the bird is an עולה. רבה's rule is not touched.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge assumed a bird חטאת can never be done above. In fact pinching anywhere on the altar is valid after the fact, so the intent is not visibly false.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Undermining the premise of the challenge: the place of pinching does not identify the offering.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Pinching above proves the bird is an עולה, so by רבה's rule the חטאת intent should be harmless and the bird should count for its owner.
steps.terutzMaskana: A bird חטאת pinched anywhere on the מזבח is valid after the fact, so pinching above proves nothing. The wrong intent is not recognizable, and רבה's rule stands.

steps.title: A bird burnt offering whose blood was squeezed above for the sake of a sin offering
steps.stepSummary: If a wrong intent that the act proves false does no harm, then a bird עולה whose blood was squeezed out above, with intent for a חטאת העוף, should be accepted. Squeezing above proves it is an עולה, because a חטאת העוף gets its blood sprinkled below.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bird burnt offering whose blood the כהן squeezed out above, for the sake of a bird sin offering, should be accepted. Its actions prove that it is a bird burnt offering, because if it were a bird sin offering, he would have sprinkled its blood below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge against רבה's rule, now using the blood service of a bird instead of the pinching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pinching case was pushed away because a חטאת העוף pinched above is also valid after the fact, so pinching above proved nothing. Blood is different: an עולת העוף has its blood squeezed out on the wall above, and a חטאת העוף has its blood sprinkled below. So squeezing above clearly shows this is an עולה, and by רבה's rule the wrong intent should not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: Squeezing the bird's blood out against the altar wall
Sprinkling the blood, the main blood service of a חטאת העוף

phrases.english: A bird burnt offering whose blood he squeezed out above
phrases.notes: "Above" means above the red line on the מזבח, where the blood of a bird עולה belongs.

phrases.english: for the sake of a bird sin offering, should be accepted
its actions prove about it
that it is a bird burnt offering
for if it were a bird sin offering
he would have performed sprinkling on it below

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹלַת הָעוֹף שֶׁמִּיצָּה דָּמָהּ לְמַעְלָה לְשֵׁם חַטַּאת הָעוֹף תְּרַצֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the pinching challenge in Step 20 was pushed away in Step 21, the גמרא raises the next challenge from its list, now about the blood service.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's rule that a wrong intent proven false by the act itself does not disqualify the קרבן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Squeezing blood above is done only for an עולה, while a חטאת העוף gets sprinkling below. So the act clearly proves this is an עולה, and by רבה's rule the קרבן should be accepted. The challenge assumes this is not the known הלכה.
